churn.def: A customer who stops using Expresso during the observation window (the CHURN label in the data).

probability.def: The model's estimate (0-100%) that a customer will churn. It is a score, not a certainty.

roc_auc.def: The chance that the model ranks a random churner above a random non-churner. 0.5 is a coin flip, 1.0 is perfect.

pp.def: The arithmetic difference between two percentages: 20% to 25% is +5 pp (a 25% relative increase).

segment.def: A group of customers with similar usage and value, found by clustering behaviour.

reason_code.def: A feature that pushed one customer's predicted risk up or down, read from the model's own contribution values.

decile.def: Customers ranked by probability and cut into ten equal groups. Decile 1 is the riskiest 10%.

lift.def: How many times more churners a targeted group contains than a random group of the same size.

psi.def: Population Stability Index: how far a column's distribution has moved from training. Below 0.1 is stable, above 0.25 is a big shift.

exploratory_band.def: Low / Medium / High labels from thresholds you choose. Not approved by the business.

silent.name: Silent / Inactive
silent.blurb: Almost no recorded usage, recharges or revenue in the 90-day window.
actions: Prioritize targeted reactivation campaigns for customers with previous value potential.
Investigate the main causes of inactivity before applying retention incentives.
Use controlled recharge or usage incentives to test customer re-engagement.
Differentiate potentially recoverable customers from persistently inactive, zero-value accounts.

high_value.name: High-Value Active
high_value.blurb: Frequent recharges, high revenue and activity on most days.
actions: Prioritize value protection because this segment contributes a disproportionate share of portfolio revenue.
Use proactive service-recovery interventions when activity or recharge behaviour starts declining.
Consider loyalty benefits and personalized offers to reinforce retention.
Monitor changes in regularity, recharge frequency and usage as potential early-warning indicators.

data_engaged.name: Data-Engaged
data_engaged.blurb: Nearly all use mobile data; solid revenue and regular activity.
actions: Strengthen retention through targeted data-bundle and digital-service offers.
Use cross-selling opportunities that complement existing high data adoption.
Encourage higher recharge frequency and longer-duration data packages.
Monitor declining data usage as a potential early sign of disengagement.

light_active.name: Light Active
light_active.blurb: Moderate activity, small recharges, calls mostly to other networks.
actions: Increase customer engagement through affordable targeted bundles and recharge incentives.
Promote migration toward higher-value products based on observed usage behaviour.
Use personalized campaigns to increase activity frequency and active days.
Monitor customers whose activity declines toward the Low-Engagement segment.

low_engagement.name: Low-Engagement
low_engagement.blurb: Few active days and little revenue: one step away from going silent.
actions: Prioritize early retention intervention before customers become fully inactive.
Use targeted reactivation or low-cost engagement offers.
Investigate barriers to recharge, data adoption and regular usage.
Monitor migration toward the Silent / Inactive segment as an early-warning signal.

exec.highest_churn: {segment} churns at {rate}, {multiple}× the portfolio rate, and holds {share} of all churners. Reactivation, not discounting, is the lever here.
exec.revenue_concentration: {segment} generates {rev} of revenue from {cust} of customers, and only {rate} of them churn. Protecting this group protects the business.
exec.value_mismatch: {churners} of churners come from {n} segment(s) that produce only {revenue} of revenue. Retention budgets should be weighted by value, not by headcount.
exec.value_exposure: {segment} carries the most revenue exposed to churn: {rev} of revenue at a {rate} churn rate. It is the best candidate for proactive retention.
exec.activity_gap: Activity separates stayers from leavers: {best} customers are active a median {best_days} days in 90, versus {worst_days} for {worst}.

REGION.name: Region
REGION.desc: Customer's home region in Senegal. Empty for many inactive customers.

TENURE.name: Tenure
TENURE.desc: How long the customer has been with Expresso, in bands from 3-6 months to over 24 months.

MONTANT.name: Recharge amount
MONTANT.desc: Total top-up amount over the period, in FCFA.

FREQUENCE_RECH.name: Number of recharges
FREQUENCE_RECH.desc: How many times the customer topped up.

REVENUE.name: Monthly revenue
REVENUE.desc: Monthly income generated by the customer, in FCFA.

ARPU_SEGMENT.name: ARPU
ARPU_SEGMENT.desc: Average revenue per user: income over 90 days divided by 3.

FREQUENCE.name: Revenue events
FREQUENCE.desc: Number of times the customer generated income.

DATA_VOLUME.name: Data usage
DATA_VOLUME.desc: Number of mobile data connections / data volume used.

ON_NET.name: On-net calls
ON_NET.desc: Calls from Expresso to Expresso numbers.

ORANGE.name: Calls to Orange
ORANGE.desc: Calls to the Orange network (a competitor).

TIGO.name: Calls to Tigo
TIGO.desc: Calls to the Tigo network (a competitor).

MRG.name: MRG flag
MRG.desc: Marker for a customer who is going (constant 'NO' in the training data).

REGULARITY.name: Active days (of 90)
REGULARITY.desc: Number of days the customer was active in the last 90 days.

TOP_PACK.name: Most used pack
TOP_PACK.desc: The bundle/pack the customer activated most often.

FREQ_TOP_PACK.name: Top-pack activations
FREQ_TOP_PACK.desc: Number of times the customer activated their top pack.

MISSING_COUNT.name: Empty usage fields
MISSING_COUNT.desc: How many usage fields are empty for the customer (more empty fields = less activity).

REVENUE_PER_RECHARGE.name: Revenue per recharge
REVENUE_PER_RECHARGE.desc: Monthly revenue divided by the number of recharges.

DATA_SHARE.name: Data per unit of revenue
DATA_SHARE.desc: Data usage divided by monthly revenue.

user_id.name: Customer ID
user_id.desc: Unique customer identifier (not used by the model).

CHURN.name: Churn label
CHURN.desc: 1 if the customer churned, 0 otherwise (training data and evaluation files only).

feat_kind.log: log(1 + value), compresses very large usage values
feat_kind.missing: 1 if the raw value is empty, else 0
feat_kind.region_missing: 1 if region is empty (one-hot; overwrites the empty-region indicator of the same name)
feat_kind.region_unseen: 1 if the region is not one of the 14 known regions
feat_kind.onehot: 1 if the customer is in this region, else 0
feat_kind.ordinal: Tenure band as an ordered number (0 = 3-6 months … 7 = over 24 months)
feat_kind.freq: Share of training customers with the same top pack (rare packs pooled as 'Other')
feat_kind.missing_count: Count of empty numeric usage fields

exec.title: Executive Dashboard
exec.sub: Where churn concentrates, where the revenue is, and what the numbers say to do. Every figure is computed from the segment profiles and model metadata.

bubble.title: Churn vs size vs value
bubble.sub: Each bubble is a segment: further right = more customers, higher = more churn, bigger = more revenue.
bubble.so_what: {worst} churns at {worst_rate} but brings only {worst_rev} of revenue, while {top} brings {top_rev} of revenue at {top_rate} churn: reactivate the top-left, protect the big bubble at the bottom.

treemap.title: Customers by segment
treemap.sub: Tile size = customers, colour = churn rate.
treemap.so_what: {big} is the largest group ({share} of customers) with a {rate} churn rate; the colour scale shows where leavers concentrate.

share.title: Share of churners vs share of revenue
share.sub: Who leaves compared with who pays.
share.so_what: {seg} accounts for {churners} of churners but only {rev} of revenue: counting churners alone would point the budget at the least valuable customers.

insights.title: Executive insights
insights.sub: Written automatically from the segment numbers above, so they update if the artifacts change.

drivers.title: What drives the model's predictions
drivers.sub: LightGBM gain importance, with engineered features grouped back to the raw Expresso column they come from.
drivers.so_what: {a} and {b} together explain {share} of the model's total gain: whether a customer's data is recorded at all, and how many days they are active, separate leavers from stayers far more than tariffs do.
drivers.more: Open Model & Explainability for the full breakdown

segx.title: Segment Explorer
segx.sub: Five behavioural segments found by clustering usage, recharges and revenue. Compare any two, benchmark them against the portfolio and read the recommended plays.

compare.title: Compare two segments
compare.sub: Pick any two segments to put side by side.

radar.title: Behaviour profile
radar.sub: Each axis is scaled to the highest segment (100 = highest of the five), so shapes are comparable.
radar.empty: Pick at least one segment to draw the radar.
radar.so_what: {high} customers are active a median {hd} days in 90 against {ld} for {low}: activity is the clearest behavioural gap between segments.

bench.title: Benchmark against the portfolio
bench.sub: Green ▲ = better than the portfolio, red ▼ = worse. For churn, lower is better.
bench.value_gap_help: Positive: the segment earns more than its headcount share (above-average value per customer).
bench.caption: Portfolio benchmarks (customer-weighted): churn {churn}, active days {days}, data users {data}, recharges {rech}.

interp.title: Management interpretation
interp.sub: Generated from the gaps above with fixed rules (±5 pp churn, ±5 days activity, ±10 pp data, ±10 pp value).
interp.churn_above: Churn is {gap} percentage points above the portfolio benchmark: a priority segment for retention or reactivation.
interp.churn_below: Churn is {gap} percentage points below the portfolio benchmark: relatively strong retention.
interp.churn_aligned: Churn is broadly in line with the portfolio benchmark ({gap}).
interp.active_below: Activity is {gap} active days below the portfolio benchmark: weaker engagement.
interp.active_above: Activity is {gap} active days above the portfolio benchmark: stronger engagement.
interp.data_below: Data adoption is {gap} points below the portfolio benchmark: room for targeted data-bundle campaigns.
interp.data_above: Data adoption is {gap} points above the portfolio benchmark: a strongly digital customer group.
interp.value_high: The segment is {cust} of customers but {rev} of revenue: value protection is a management priority.
interp.value_low: The segment is {cust} of customers but only {rev} of revenue: relatively low commercial value.
interp.caption: Interpretations support prioritisation; they do not replace business judgement or approved customer-treatment policies.

actions.title: Recommended management actions
actions.sub: The team's playbook for each segment.
actions.caption: Recommended actions are management strategies based on segment behaviour, not model outputs. Validate them against campaign economics, treatment policies and capacity.

matrix.title: Strategy matrix
matrix.sub: Churn rate against revenue share. Move the cut-offs to test how robust each segment's placement is.
matrix.rev_cut_help: Default: an equal share (100% ÷ number of segments).
matrix.so_what_protect: {segs} combine high value with high churn: they are first in line for retention budget.
matrix.so_what_none: No segment is both high-value and high-churn at these cut-offs. Keep {seg} safe with early-warning monitoring and spend reactivation effort on {react}.

protect.name: Protect
protect.desc: High value, high churn: spend retention budget here first.

grow.name: Grow
grow.desc: High value, low churn: loyalty, upsell and early-warning monitoring.

reactivate.name: Reactivate
reactivate.desc: Low value, high churn: low-cost, automated reactivation; test before scaling.

deprioritise.name: Deprioritise
deprioritise.desc: Low value, low churn: no special spend; nudge toward higher-value products.

cc.title: Customer Check
cc.sub: Score a single customer with the deployed model, see the reasons behind the score and get a suggested next action.

presets.title: Start from a typical customer
presets.sub: Fill the form with the median customer of a segment, then adjust.
presets.help: Loads that segment's medians into the form and scores it.
presets.note_profile: Other usage fields are not in segment_profiles.csv, so they are left as 'not recorded'. Region and tenure keep your current choice.
presets.note_eda: All fields come from per-segment medians in eda_summary.json.

form.customer_id_help: Any label for this customer. It is not used by the model.
form.not_recorded_help: Tick when the value is empty in the customer's record. Empty values carry information for the model.
form.mrg_note: MRG is always 'NO' in the training data and is not used by the model, so it is fixed.

cc.hint_run: Pick a typical customer above or fill the form, then press 'Score this customer'.

result.title: Result for {id}
result.sub: The model's churn probability, compared with the portfolio.
result.multiple_help: This customer's probability divided by the portfolio churn rate.
result.segment_help: Assigned with the bundle's segmentation model (the silent-customer rule is reconstructed from its config).
result.no_bands: No Low / Medium / High label is shown: business risk thresholds have not been approved. A typical (median) customer usually scores below its segment's average churn rate, because churn concentrates among the least active members.

why.title: Why this score
why.raw_help: Off: engineered features are grouped by the raw column they come from. On: all 69 model features.
why.so_what: {name} {dir} this customer's risk the most. Red bars push toward churn, blue bars pull away from it.

reasons.title: In plain words
reasons.sub: The five biggest reason codes, from the model's own contribution values.

nba.title: Next best action
nba.sub: Suggestions driven by the reason codes and profile.
nba.caption: Business suggestions, not model output. Check offers against campaign policy and budget.

cc.to_whatif: Try changes in the What-If Simulator

val.REGULARITY: Active on {v} of the last 90 days
val.REGION_unseen: Region '{v}' is not one the model knows

low_risk.title: No retention spend needed
low_risk.body: Risk is well below the portfolio rate. Keep this customer in normal loyalty communications.

vip_call.title: Priority call
vip_call.body: High revenue at above-average risk: have the retention desk call within 48 hours with a personalised offer.

dormant.title: Reactivate a dormant line
dormant.body: Most usage fields are empty. Send a low-cost reactivation offer (e.g. bonus credit on the next recharge) and track whether the line wakes up.

verify_record.title: Complete the customer record
verify_record.body: No region is recorded, which the model reads as a strong churn signal. Verify the record; a missing profile often means an inactive or secondary SIM.

activity.title: Activity nudge
activity.body: Few active days drive this score. A short, time-limited usage bonus can bring activity back up; follow up after two weeks.

recharge.title: Recharge incentive
recharge.body: Recharge behaviour pushes risk up. Offer bonus credit on the next recharges or an automatic recharge plan.

data.title: Data trial
data.body: Data usage pushes risk up. A small, cheap data bundle trial can build a data habit that keeps customers on the network.

onnet.title: On-net bundle
onnet.body: Low on-net calling pushes risk up. An on-net calling bundle strengthens ties within the Expresso network.

allnet.title: All-net bundle
allnet.body: Calls to competitor networks push risk up. An all-net pack reduces the pull to switch to Orange or Tigo.

pack.title: Pack fit review
pack.body: The customer's pack pattern pushes risk up. Suggest a pack that better matches their usage.

monitor.title: Monitor
monitor.body: No single behaviour stands out. Keep the customer under watch and rescore next period.

wi.title: What-If Simulator
wi.sub: Change one customer's behaviour and see how the churn probability would move. This shows how the model responds; it does not prove that changing a behaviour causes a customer to stay.

source.label: Starting customer
source.no_last: Tip: score someone on Customer Check first to start from that customer here.

levers.title: Levers
levers.sub: The behaviours a retention offer could plausibly influence.
levers.ranges_eda: Slider ranges come from the training distribution (eda_summary.json).
levers.ranges_fallback: Slider ranges scale with this customer's values and the segment medians. Export eda_summary.json to use the training distribution instead.

compare.title: Baseline vs scenario
compare.sub: Same customer, before and after your changes.

sweep.title: Which lever helps most?
sweep.sub: Each lever is swept across its range while everything else stays at the scenario values (an individual partial-dependence curve).
sweep.so_what: {name} is the strongest lever for this customer: moving it to about {value} lowers the probability by up to {gain} points.
sweep.so_what_none: No single lever lowers this customer's probability within the ranges shown.
sweep.curve_so_what: The lowest probability on this curve is {p}, at {name} ≈ {value}. Flat stretches mean the model is insensitive there.
sweep.caveat: Curves show model sensitivity for this one customer, holding everything else fixed. Real behaviours move together, so treat these as directions, not forecasts.
